title: Multi agent feature stream run
first_prompt:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

<system-reminder>
<tools-used-before-summary>Ag

commits.summary: application-core reuse R1: the native property cache, a property projection of the canonical claim in the existing proof store
commits.body:
prove --cache DIR now keeps a property check's verified and refuted results in the regression proofs' store (lib/src/reuse.rs), keyed by the same canonical claim digest. The claim projects the target's parameters, the closure of the target and of every constructor its inputs, result and declared exceptions are made with, the assumption, assertion, throws clauses, the meaning of \old, the null and alias choices, any construction plan, the bounds and the checker's settings. A first assumption marks it a property claim, so it never shares a key with a regression claim of the same target. Every field of property::Options is named in the projection; an unknown one, or an engine other than the own checker, refuses the check under --cache instead of keying without it. A verified hit gives back the stored outcome and statement, marked as reused. A refutation is stored with the harness it was found in, and reused only once its witness fails that harness again on the current classes. Nothing unresolved is stored.

Verified inline: lib/tests/reuse.rs (7 tests, on the frozen quote fixture and small builds, native engine, no JBMC): exact hits of both kinds, a stale stored witness proved again, an input's changed constructor invalidating the proof of an unchanged method (the test fails with the constructor roots taken out), a key per assertion, assumption, throws clause, domain, bound and plan history, none for an unrelated change. The contract's R1 now verifies cold and on the rerun; 230 unit tests, tests/application_core.rs and tests/summaries.rs pass, clippy is clean. Interface requests for property.rs and main.rs are under the stream brief's Progress.

commits.summary: application-core reuse J3: a planned domain's plans and a modelled call's model in the claim key, digested whole as their strict types
commits.body:
The claim key's projection (lib/src/spec/cache.rs) refused every claim with a planned domain or a call model as uncacheable, since Phase 0 added those parts without registering them. TYPED now names domain.made_by.before/after (construction plans) and environment.calls[].model (a call model): each is digested whole once it reads back exactly as its type of spec::plans, which refuses every undeclared field and variant, so nothing in them is left out of the key and an undeclared field still makes the claim uncacheable by name.

Verified inline: three new tests in lib/tests/reuse.rs. The 8 frozen claims of tests/fixtures/application-core each get a distinct key; 27 changes to their histories (setup calls, constructors, factories, setup bounds, one version's plan alone), model outcomes (results, exceptions, coupling, key, bound) and value bounds (String and list lengths, nullability, evidence levels, element kinds) each give a new key; undeclared fields, an unknown variant and a non-canonical plan are refused. The integration contract's J3 now passes on distinct keys instead of on the refusal. 230 unit tests and the contract, summaries, heap, effects and foundations suites pass.

Also recorded under Progress: an unsound regression-cache hit the objects stream found in proof_cache.rs (an inner object's constructor is missing from the closure's roots), which is this stream's next piece of work.

commits.summary: application-core reuse: a regression claim's closure rooted at every constructor its harness calls, an inner object's included
commits.body:
proof_cache::Regression::claim rooted each version's closure at a made object's own constructor only, not at the constructors of the objects it is made from, which the harness calls too. So a build that changed only an inner constructor reused another build's verified result: get(new Wrap(new Inner(v), k)), whose Inner constructor stores v + 1 in one build, reused a rewrite's proof though get returns one more. The objects stream found it (their ignored test an_inner_objects_constructor_is_part_of_the_cached_claim). The claim now roots both versions, and a previous version's receiver and records, at every constructor RecordType::constructors lists.

Reproducer first: tests/reuse.rs's an_inner_objects_constructor_in_either_version_is_part_of_a_regression_claim failed before the fix with an exact hit on the changed build. It now checks that a rewrite is verified and reused on an unchanged rerun, and that a change to the inner constructor after, and then before, misses the cache and is refuted. Also fixed: tests/reuse.rs compiled each build into a shared directory it removed first, so parallel tests could remove each other's classes. Each build is now compiled once per run. Verified inline: tests/reuse.rs (11 tests, three runs), the 230 unit tests, and the application_core, compare, effects, foundations, heap, observations and summaries suites. The proof_cache module doc and lib/README.md say which constructors are roots.

commits.summary: application-core reuse R2: a read-only helper's footprint proved from its bytecode, lifted over it, and summarized from a proof of its own
commits.body:
R2's first part, in lib/src/reuse/footprint.rs (a submodule of reuse.rs, so no shared file changed), reuse::summarize and proof_cache::lifted_proof. footprint::footprint establishes a heap helper's read footprint from its bytecode rather than listing likely reads. The helper is an instance method no application class overrides, with primitive parameters and result. The only reference it handles is its receiver, loaded only to read a primitive field at once, and its static callees are walked under the same rules with no reference at all. So its getfields are all it reads of the heap, and since it writes nothing its outcome is a function of those fields' values and its arguments. The brief's exclusions (a write, an allocation, an exception of its own, a static field, an external call, a call on an object, an override, recursion, an escaping reference, an array) are each refused by name, and so are a division by anything but a non-zero constant, a switch and floating point.

footprint::lift is the explicit representation adapter: the helper as a static method of its own class over its arguments and then the values of the fields either version reads, with each field read replaced by a parameter. reuse::summarize proves the two versions' lifted helpers equal by a regression check of their own, under the caller's cache, engine and bounds and in the proof stack that keeps dependency proofs acyclic. It gives a spec::plans::Summary naming the proof's claim key, the fields and arguments read, the domain (every value of them, whatever else a receiver holds), and the proofs it rests on. A helper whose versions differ, or whose versions read fields the other's receiver doesn't declare alike, has none. No caller applies a summary yet; that, with the caller's claim carrying the summaries it used, is the next part.

Verified inline with a new tests/reuse_summaries.rs (5 tests): the frozen quote fixture's fee reads feeCents before and after, and its helper-extra-field defect also reads floorCents; 17 helpers outside the category are each refused in the words of their case; the lifting agrees with the helper on a real JVM over 560 cases, lifted over one field more than it reads; fee's summary has its proof verified in the cache, and an exact rerun gives the same summary with nothing new stored; the extra read and a layout change get no summary. The 231 unit tests, tests/reuse.rs (11), application_core (14), summaries, compare, heap, effects and foundations pass. Found: the lifted proof is positional in the fields' values, so a caller's claim must carry the whole summary (its reads), not only the proof's key; this is recorded under Progress for the next part. The contract's R2 row still stops at the objects stream's receiver refusal, as it checks fee through the plain regression entry point.

commits.summary: application-core reuse R2: a changed caller reuses a read-only helper's summary at each call, through adapters that read the receiver there
commits.body:
Under --cache and the own checker, shared::plan_with now asks for a summary of each changed instance method both versions of a regression target call, declared by the same class. proof_cache::Helpers sends such a method to reuse::application, which makes the summary (its lifted proof from the cache, or proved now) and two call-site adapters (reuse::footprint::adapters). shared::substitute then rewrites every call of the helper, in both versions, into a static call of that version's adapter. The adapter reads each footprint field from the actual receiver as its own version lays it out, and calls the new version's lifted helper, so both versions call one function of the same values. Because the summary's proof covers every value of the fields and arguments, reading them at the call discharges applicability on the actual pre-call state: a receiver mutated between two calls is read twice, and a write through an aliasing parameter is seen. The caller's claim carries the whole summary as an assumption of kind summary, basis proved, with its proof's key (J3's helper assumptions). A helper with no summary keeps its body in both versions, with a note saying why.

Verified inline in lib/tests/reuse_summaries.rs (5 new tests, 10 in all, three runs). A tariff's rewritten fee is proved on its own, then reused by three changed callers, which are verified: one call, two calls around a mutation, and a write through another parameter with and without may_alias. A stale read after a mutation, and a read before an aliased write, are refuted with the summary applied, and their witnesses replay. A helper that reads an extra field, and helper versions that agree only on constructor-made receivers, get no summary. Their callers keep the body: the first is refuted, the second verified for a single call in the constructor domain and refuted, replayed, once a second call follows a lowered fee. On a JVM with -Xverify:all, the classes with the summary applied agree with the versions as written over a grid. Also passing: the 231 unit tests, reuse (11), application_core (14), summaries (40), compare, heap (49), effects (18), foundations (5) and observations (12). The contract's R2 row still stops at the objects stream's construction::receiver, since the quote's target is an instance method. That is for the merge.

commits.summary: application-core reuse R3: a small compare run timed stage by stage around the proof cache, cold, rerun and a defect (verification pending)
commits.body:
R3 of llm-dlc/loops/application-core-reuse.md measures before it adds any cache of preparation. A new ledger (lib/src/reuse/preparation.rs) times, while a caller records one, the proof cache's own steps where they run, all in this stream's files: shared::plan_with, each helper's own proof, the claim key with both versions' closures digested, the lookup, the store, a witness replayed, and each proof's checker runs with their phases, read at the store. preparation::proofs splits a ledger into proofs and gives each the stretch before its first span, so that what no hook covers (relocating, decoding the target's classes, the layout, the harness) is placed proof by proof without a hook in another stream's file. Nothing is recorded without a ledger.

The benchmark lib/tests/preparation.rs (ignored inline) runs compare on the joint example's builds (examples 190, 191) cold, as an unchanged rerun, on the offset defect cold and as its rerun, in process under the ledger and as the compare process build.py runs. It also times one by one the stages a run repeats: javac per build, decoding and relocating a build, alignment, the specs, opening the JDK image, writing the models, the models' digest and the binary's digest. Queued as job 20261108-060410-application-core-reuse-r3-a-small-compar for the release figures, which come back as lib/benchmark/preparation/preparation.json and .md.

A debug smoke run inline (1 repeat): a rerun of the 5 proofs took 810 ms, 726 ms of it before the lookups. Relocating took 0.8 ms and decoding the build 0.3 ms, while opening the JDK image took 31 ms each time, and every class path with the JDK opens it again. That is the likely repeated stage; the job decides. Verified inline: the ledger's 2 unit tests (233 in all), and reuse, reuse_summaries, compare, application_core, summaries, effects, heap, foundations and observations all pass. Also recorded under Progress: the integration check's conflict in lib/README.md (all four streams' additions), which is the merge's to take whole.

commits.summary: application-core reuse R2: a read-only helper's summary over the primitive arrays its receiver's fields hold, applied only within its bound
commits.body:
R2's bounded reads of primitive arrays, after the field-only case (llm-dlc/loops/application-core-reuse.md). The footprint (lib/src/reuse/footprint.rs) now accepts a field holding a one-dimensional non-floating primitive array, read by its length and elements. A flow over every path of the helper's code, locals included, proves every reference it handles is its receiver or such an array, kept only in a local and used only by arraylength and an element load of its own type. A write, passing it on, comparing or null-testing it, two arrays meeting at a join, and arrays of floats, references or arrays are each refused by name. A read out of bounds throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, an outcome the summary's proof compares: this departs from the brief's 'total' for the field case, recorded for review.

The lifted helper takes the array itself. Since the proof's harness makes no null array and none over the claim's bound, the summary carries facts (this.tiers != null, this.tiers.length <= 8). Each version's adapter checks them on the actual receiver at each call and, where one fails, calls its own version's helper as written instead. Each adapter is now a class of its own in its version's package, so it reaches package-private members legally.

Verified inline in tests/reuse_summaries.rs, 4 new tests (14 in all, three runs): eight refusals; a lifted array helper agreeing with the helper on a JVM over 72 cases, 54 out of bounds; a for-each rewrite's summary reused by five changed callers, through a tier mutated via the field and via the caller's alias (each verified, and refuted and replayed in a stale defect), and through a 10-element and a null array, where the body is kept; a helper charging one tier more refused, its caller refuted; and a helper whose versions differ only past the bound, whose caller on 10 elements is refuted and replayed. With the guard taken out for a check, that caller was verified, the defect hidden. On a JVM with -Xverify:all, the applied classes agree with the versions as written. The 233 unit tests and reuse, summaries, application_core, compare, heap, effects and foundations pass. R3's job 20261108-060410 has come back passed; deciding R3 from it is next.

commits.summary: application-core reuse R3: the JDK image's table of classes built once per process and shared, keyed by its index (verification pending)
commits.body:
R3's measurement (job 20261108-060410, passed, release, on the joint example's builds) put an unchanged compare rerun at 209.8 ms in process and 290.3 ms as a process, 185.4 ms of it before the proofs' lookups, and opening the JDK image (lib/modules) at 6.26 ms. Counted with an open() shim, a rerun opens the image 28 times and a cold run 50: every class path with the JDK opens it, and each open built the table of every class in the image, about 175 ms of the rerun. No other repeated stage is above a millisecond (decoding and relocating a build, the models' digest and writing them), and compilation is reported apart (javac 0.4 s per build).

So that table is the one product of preparation now cached. JImage::open still reads the file's header and index each time, and takes the table built earlier in the same process from the same index bytes, if any (up to 4 indexes). It is keyed by the index's bytes themselves, not by a path, size or time, so an image changed in place or another JDK at the same path gets its own. Resources are still read from the file opened, and no proof key changes. jimage.rs is in no stream's ownership row and no stream has touched it since the fork. The change is internal, with no signature moved. That departs from the brief's Progress, which planned an interface request, and is recorded there for review.

Verified inline: a new unit test, which could not pass before, shows that two opens share the table and read the same class. A copy of the index alone elsewhere shares it too, and a copy with java/lang/Object renamed by one byte gets its own table and leaves the shared one intact. The benchmark run once in debug: an unchanged rerun went from 846 ms to 37 ms in process, with the same verdicts. Also passing: the 234 unit tests and the reuse (11), reuse_summaries (14), compare, application_core (14), summaries (40), effects (18), heap (49), foundations (5) and observations (12) suites. The benchmark now also times an open whose index is new apart from one that shares the table. Job 20261108-063259 reruns it in release into lib/benchmark/preparation/shared-image.json beside the first report.

commits.summary: Loops record why they stop (the default workspace's kppsnzyn, copied here for the rerun)
commits.body: This stream runs its own workspace's copy of feature-loop.sh, so the fix made in the default workspace as change kppsnzyn is committed here unchanged, byte for byte, before run-streams.sh reruns this stream. A session that decides to stop while this brief's status still says working now gets a turn to set the status and commit it, and the cycle instruction asks for the status line to be kept current. The files are identical to kppsnzyn's, so the merge takes them without a conflict. Verified there (bash -n and a stubbed test of the new functions).

commits.summary: application-core reuse R3 done: the shared JDK image table's release figures, read from job 20261108-063259
commits.body:
Job 20261108-063259 (passed at 3841df5e, 3m22s, peak 1.7 GiB) ran the same release benchmark as job 20261108-060410, with the JDK image's table of classes now shared within the process. It reached the same verdicts in all four scenarios, both in process and as a process. Medians of 7, before the cache and with it: an unchanged rerun took 209.8 ms and now 8.6 ms in process (290.3 and 66.1 ms as a process), the cold run 460.6 and 65.6 ms, the defect's cold run 2217 and 1576 ms (solving 1723 and 1484 ms), and its rerun 265.3 and 31.9 ms. An open that builds the table takes 7.89 ms, and one that shares it 0.06 ms. javac still takes about 0.4 s per build, so compilation outweighs a whole rerun: the cut is to preparation, not to proving a change. The runner committed the reports (lib/benchmark/preparation/shared-image.*) in the default workspace, and they reach this branch at the merge.

R3's record in the brief's Progress now holds these figures, and lib/README.md's paragraph on preparation gives them in place of the pending note. Verified by reading both jobs' reports in full and comparing their verdicts. Nothing else changed: the README edit is prose only. Also found: the benchmark lacks the acceptance contract's unrelated edit and safe helper rewrite. Without the helper rewrite, it can't show helper evidence apart from exact hits, as the brief's Acceptance asks. Adding them is next, so that J4 at the merge runs the full set.

commits.summary: application-core reuse J4: the cost benchmark gets an unrelated edit and a safe helper rewrite, the contract's last two cases (verification pending)
commits.body:
lib/tests/preparation.rs, the ignored benchmark of R3, timed a cold compare run on the joint example's builds (examples 190 and 191), an unchanged rerun, the real defect offset and its rerun. The acceptance contract's measurement also asks for an unrelated edit and a safe rewrite of a helper, and the reuse brief asks the report to tell exact hits, helper evidence and preparation reuse apart. Two overlays on after, in a new lib/tests/fixtures/preparation/ with a README, are now run from a copy of the proof cache a cold run of after leaves: unrelated-edit adds a class nothing reaches, and helper-rewrite rewrites Pricing.discount again. The report lists, per subject, whether it was an exact hit or proved, and which helper proofs it was proved on. The benchmark asserts that the unrelated edit proves nothing again, and that in the helper rewrite total is proved again on a new proof of discount while withQuantity is an exact hit. No library code changed.

Verified with a debug smoke run inline (1 repeat, 58 s, passed): the unrelated edit gave 5 exact hits; the helper rewrite gave 1 exact hit and 4 proofs (the route, discount as a subject and as total's helper, and total on the new helper proof). The route is proved again because its effect proof's closure holds the helper's body. The release figures are job 20261108-114325-application-core-reuse-j4-the-small-comp, which writes lib/benchmark/preparation/j4.json and .md.

commits.summary: application-core reuse J4: the cost report's figures with all five cases, read from job 20261108-114325; the stream is done
commits.body:
Job 20261108-114325 (passed at 283aa75d, 3m37s, peak 1.7 GiB) ran lib/tests/preparation.rs in release with the acceptance contract's five cases on the joint example: cold, an unchanged rerun, an unrelated edit, a safe rewrite of the helper Pricing.discount, and the offset defect cold and rerun. Every repeat and the process reached the expected verdicts, and every assertion held. Medians of 7, as a process: cold 127.0 ms, rerun 62.5, unrelated edit 64.4 (5 exact hits), helper rewrite 138.7 (1 exact hit, 4 proved: total on the helper's new proof, named by key, and the route again because its effect proof's closure holds the helper's body), defect cold 1687.6 (1364 ms solving) and its rerun 83.7. The edited build's javac, about 400 ms, is 74-87% of every scenario with compilation except the defect's cold run. So the gain is to a rerun's preparation, not a whole build's, and helper evidence is reused by key, not made cheaper to obtain. The runner committed the reports (lib/benchmark/preparation/j4.*) in the default workspace; they reach this branch at the merge.

The brief's Progress records the figures, the three kinds of reuse apart, and two items for the main loop's for-review list: effect proofs don't use helper evidence, and the R2 contract row still stops at the objects stream's construction::receiver until the merge. lib/README.md's preparation paragraph gives the two new cases. Verified by reading the job's report, its log and j4.json's verdicts in full; the README change is prose only. The stream's items are done (R1, R2, R3's justified outcome, J3, and J4's report), with R4 left out as the brief allows, so the status is done. J4's rerun on the merged revision is the main loop's Phase 5, and the interface requests recorded under R1 wait for the merge.
The application-core reconcile (llm-dlc/loops/application-core.md, step 3): the reuse stream's last turns recorded on its branch, after its last commit, before the merge.
